s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment
salient_findings: Episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
key_facts: Woman in her mid-60s
Initial carpal tunnel release surgery
Recurring tremors
Referred to a neurologist 7 months later
Developed progressive right-sided weakness over 3 months
Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas
No contrast enhancement on T1-weighted MRI
Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells
Cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells
Bone marrow was negative for lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells and cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas without contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas

shortlist.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas

shortlist.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive right-sided weakness, dysarthria, and gait instability

raw.rationale: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and the brain biopsy showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells are strong evidence for Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma. The brain MRI findings of hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas without contrast enhancement are also consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: Typically associated with immunocompromised state and presence of JC virus, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis
rejected.why: Usually presents with discrete episodes of neurological dysfunction and lesions on MRI that are typically periventricular, juxtacortical, or infratentorial, which does not match the diffuse and progressive nature of this case

rejected.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: Typically a monophasic illness with rapid progression and often associated with recent viral infection or vaccination, which is not indicated in the case

rejected.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
rejected.why: A neurodegenerative disorder that typically presents with asymmetric parkinsonism, dystonia, and myoclonus, which does not match the rapid progression and widespread lesions seen in this case
